questions.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
questions.stem:
The V – I characteristics of a solar cell is shown in the figure.
(a) What do the points P and Q represent ?
(b) Give the circuit diagram for a solar cell.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — the whole of part (a) is a reading off the drawing: P and Q are LABELS THAT EXIST ONLY IN THE FIGURE and the stem never says where either sits, so the row is unanswerable without it. Withheld deliberately from the stem: which axis each point lies on, because that IS the answer (the marking scheme keys P = open-circuit potential difference / emf and Q = short-circuit current, which follow from nothing but their positions). What may safely be said, and is all that is needed to crop it: a V–I graph with the current axis vertical (labelled I) and the voltage axis horizontal (labelled V, arrowed both ways), one curve, and the two labelled points P and Q on it. Page idx 4.

questions.subtopic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation and the Photon
questions.stem: Photoelectric emission occurs when a surface is irradiated with the radiation of frequency (i) \(v_1\), and (ii) \(v_2\). The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted in the two cases are K and 2K respectively. Obtain the expression for the threshold frequency for the surface.
questions._flag: The two frequencies are printed as an italic LATIN 'v' with a subscript, not the Greek nu the quantity normally carries. Transcribed AS PRINTED. Re-measured on THIS paper's own PDF rather than inherited from the 55/2/1 transcription, with a probe that self-tests first: on idx 4 the Symbol-font Greek DROPS from the text layer entirely (the alpha of Q3(a), both thetas and both degree signs all extract as nothing) while these two characters survive extraction as ASCII 'v' — so they are set in the body font, i.e. Latin. The rendered glyph at 5x agrees. No effect on answerability; the quantity is unambiguously frequency.

questions.stem:
(a) Depict the variation of the potential energy of a pair of nucleons with the separation between them.
(b) Imagine the fission of a \({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}\) into two equal fragments of \({}^{28}_{13}\mathrm{Al}\) nucleus. Is the fission energetically possible ? Justify your answer by working out Q value of the process.
Given : \(m\left({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}\right) = 55{\cdot}93494\) u, \(m\left({}^{28}_{13}\mathrm{Al}\right) = 27{\cdot}98191\) u.
questions._flag: Two observations, neither a stem defect. (1) SPANS TWO SUBTOPICS and the marking scheme splits it 1½ / 1½, so neither half dominates: part (b), the fission Q value, is filed here under 'Nuclear Energy', while part (a), the nucleon-pair potential-energy curve, belongs to the declared-but-unused subtopic 'Nuclear Force'. Recorded rather than silently picked, and filed to match the same question in the 55/2/1 set so the two dedup. (2) FOR THE LATER SOLUTION-AUTHORING STEP: the marking scheme's Total-Marks column prints 2 for this question, contradicting its own breakdown on the facing page (Graph 1½ + Mass Difference 1 + Conclusion ½ = 3) and the paper's printed 3. Marks taken as 3, per the paper and instruction (iv).

questions.stem: An equiconvex lens forms a two times enlarged real image when an object is kept 16 cm from it. The lens is cut into two identical plano-convex lenses. If the object is again kept 16 cm in front of one of these lenses, then find the nature and position of the image formed.

A ray is incident on a prism of material of refractive index \(\sqrt{2}\) at point M such that it grazes along NC after emerging from the prism, as shown in the figure.
Find :
(a) the critical angle for the prism.
(b) the angle of refraction at face AB.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — part (b) is solved from \(A = r_1 + r_2\), and the PRISM ANGLE A IS PRINTED ONLY IN THE DRAWING: the stem gives the refractive index and nothing else, never stating the apex angle nor that the prism is equilateral, so without the figure part (b) has no data at all. The figure also fixes which face the ray enters (AB, at M) and which it leaves (AC, at N), which the stem only half-implies. What may safely be said: a triangular prism ABC with apex A at the top, B bottom-left and C bottom-right, two marked angles, M labelled on side AB and N on side AC, an arrowed ray drawn from M to N inside the prism and a further arrowed ray leaving N. Withheld: the two angle VALUES and the orientation of the emergent ray relative to face AC, which are what parts (a) and (b) turn on. Page idx 6.

questions.subtopic: Line Spectra of the Hydrogen Atom
questions.stem:
An electron is in the third excited state in a hydrogen atom. It undergoes transitions to the lower energy states.
(a) What is the maximum number of spectral lines that can be emitted ?
(b) Calculate the minimum wavelength of the spectral lines emitted.
questions._flag: FOR THE LATER SOLUTION-AUTHORING STEP, not a stem defect: the marking scheme's worked answer to part (b) ends '\(\lambda = 975nm = 9.75 \times 10^{-11}\) m', and those two are not the same quantity — 975 nm is \(9{\cdot}75 \times 10^{-7}\) m. The scheme's own preceding line is right (12·75 eV for the n=4 to n=1 transition), and that energy gives \(9{\cdot}75 \times 10^{-8}\) m = 97·5 nm, so BOTH printed forms of the final value are wrong while the method above them is correct. Do not carry either figure across verbatim.

questions.context: The British physicist Thomas Young explained the interference of light using the principle of superposition of waves. He observed the interference pattern on the screen, in his experimental set-up, known now as Young's double slit experiment. The two slits \(\mathrm{S_1}\) and \(\mathrm{S_2}\) were illuminated by light from a slit S. The interference pattern consists of dark and bright bands of light. Such bands are called fringes. The distance between two consecutive bright and dark fringes is called fringe width.
questions.stem: If the screen is moved closer to the plane of slits \(\mathrm{S_1}\) and \(\mathrm{S_2}\), then the fringe width :

options.label: A
options.text: will decrease, but the intensity of bright fringe remains the same.

options.label: B
options.text: will increase, but the intensity of bright fringe decreases.

options.label: C
options.text: will decrease, but the intensity of bright fringe increases.

options.label: D
options.text: and the intensity both remain the same.
